fridge.title: Repair or Replace a Refrigerator? A Denver Guide
fridge.description: Not sure whether to fix or replace your refrigerator? How we diagnose the fault, quote the exact repair and help you compare it with a comparable new unit.
fridge.heroText: Most refrigerator problems come down to one failed part. Here is how we help you decide, with real numbers, before any work begins.
fridge.body:
The short answer

Diagnose first. A refrigerator that is warm, noisy or leaking usually has one failed part behind it, and a single part on an otherwise sound refrigerator is normally worth repairing.

Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price after diagnosis, before any work begins, and you compare that number with the price of a comparable new refrigerator. If the diagnosis points the other way, we tell you.

Repair vs. replace at a glance

How repairing compares with replacing a refrigerator. Prices are never guessed: the repair side is quoted after diagnosis, the replace side is the price of a comparable new refrigerator.
FactorRepairReplace
Cost to find out$109 service call, which covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward the repair when you approve it.The price of a comparable new refrigerator.
What the price is based onThe part that failed and the labor to replace it, quoted after diagnosis and before any work begins.The model you choose: size, features and finish set the price, not the fault.
Installation and fitThe refrigerator stays in its cutout with its water line, finish and handles unchanged.A new unit has to fit the cutout, the doorway and the water line; built-in, counter-depth and French-door models are the hardest to match.
How many major parts have failedOne failed part on an otherwise sound refrigerator is a normal repair.Several major components failing at the same time make a repair harder to justify.
Parts availabilityA part we can get is a repair we can quote.Parts that are discontinued or on a long backorder tip the decision toward replacing.
Warranty60-day parts and labor warranty on the completed repair.Whatever warranty comes with the new unit.

What to weigh before you decide

  • What failed. One part (a defrost heater or thermostat, a fan motor, a start relay, a door gasket or a water valve) is the normal case. Several major components at once is not.
  • Food at risk. A refrigerator that has stopped cooling needs a decision today. Book the diagnosis, then decide with the quote in hand instead of guessing.
  • Fit. Built-in, counter-depth and French-door models are matched to a kitchen cutout and a water line. A replacement has to fit the same space.
  • The quote against the price of a comparable new refrigerator. We give you the exact repair price after diagnosis so the comparison is real.
  • Parts availability for your model. Discontinued parts or a long backorder change the answer.

Usually worth diagnosing and repairing

These are the everyday refrigerator repairs: one failed part, replaced on site, with the refrigerator staying where it is.

  • A refrigerator not cooling while the compressor runs: usually a defrost heater or defrost thermostat, an evaporator or condenser fan motor, a damper or a temperature sensor.
  • A failed compressor start relay or capacitor on an otherwise sound refrigerator.
  • A fridge leaking water or water under the crisper drawers: a defrost drain tube, a water inlet valve or a filter housing.
  • An ice maker not making ice or a water dispenser not working on a refrigerator that otherwise works.
  • A freezer not freezing while the fresh-food side holds temperature.
  • A fridge making noise from a fan motor, or a door gasket, hinge, crisper track or leveling problem.
  • A built-in, counter-depth or French-door model that fits your kitchen cutout.

When replacement may make more sense

  • Several major components are failing at the same time.
  • The repair quote comes close to the price of a comparable new refrigerator.
  • Parts for your model are discontinued or on a long backorder.

If the diagnosis points to the sealed system (the compressor and refrigerant circuit), we explain what we found and what your options are before anything is quoted or done. Either way, you decide with the facts in front of you.

faq.q: Is it worth repairing a refrigerator that is not cooling?
faq.a: Usually yes. A refrigerator that runs but does not cool most often has one failed part: a defrost heater or defrost thermostat, an evaporator or condenser fan motor, a start relay, a damper or a temperature sensor. We replace the part on site and quote the exact repair after diagnosis, before any work begins. If several major components are failing at the same time, we tell you that instead.

faq.q: How much does it cost to find out whether my refrigerator can be repaired?
faq.a: Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price before any work begins, so you can compare it with the price of a comparable new refrigerator and decide.

faq.q: What does refrigerator repair cost in Denver?
faq.a: Typical total repair cost (parts + labor) is $150–$500 on our refrigerator repair page, depending on the part. The estimated labor by repair is listed there as labor only, parts extra, and every completed repair carries our 60-day parts and labor warranty.

faq.q: Does a built-in, counter-depth or French-door refrigerator change the decision?
faq.a: Yes. Those models are matched to a kitchen cutout and a water line, so a replacement has to fit the same space and finish. A single failed part on a built-in, counter-depth or French-door refrigerator is normally worth repairing.

faq.q: What if only the freezer or the ice maker is the problem?
faq.a: A freezer compartment that will not freeze or an ice maker that has stopped on a refrigerator that otherwise works is normally a repair, not a replacement. See our freezer repair and ice maker repair pages for those faults.

washer.title: Repair or Replace a Washer? A Denver Guide
washer.description: Leaking, not draining or not spinning? How we decide whether a washer is worth repairing, what a diagnosis costs and when a teardown repair changes the answer.
washer.heroText: Leaks, draining and spin problems are usually a single-part repair. Here is how we help you decide, with the exact price in hand.
washer.body:
The short answer

Diagnose first. A washer that leaks, will not drain or will not spin normally has one failed part behind it, and that is usually a one-visit fix on a machine whose tub, motor and drum are sound.

Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price after diagnosis, before any work begins. The decision gets a closer look when the repair falls into the Major teardown repairs group, where the tub and drum have to come apart.

Repair vs. replace at a glance

How repairing compares with replacing a washer. Prices are never guessed: the repair side is quoted after diagnosis, the replace side is the price of a comparable new washer.
FactorRepairReplace
Cost to find out$109 service call, which covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward the repair when you approve it.The price of a comparable new washer.
What the price is based onThe part that failed and the labor to replace it, quoted after diagnosis and before any work begins.The model you choose: size, features and finish set the price, not the fault.
Installation and fitThe washer stays on its hoses, drain and outlet; a front-load or top-load machine is repaired in place.A new washer has to fit the space, the door swing and the hookups; a stacked pair or a tight laundry closet limits the choice.
How many major parts have failedOne failed part on an otherwise sound washer is a normal repair.Several major components failing at the same time make a repair harder to justify.
Parts availabilityA part we can get is a repair we can quote.Parts that are discontinued or on a long backorder tip the decision toward replacing.
Warranty60-day parts and labor warranty on the completed repair.Whatever warranty comes with the new unit.

What to weigh before you decide

  • What failed. A lid switch or door lock, drain pump, inlet valve, belt or shock absorbers is one part. The tub bearing, motor and control board failing together is a different situation.
  • Which repair group it falls into. Controls & sensors and Parts & mechanical repairs are the everyday fixes. Major teardown repairs (tub bearing, spider arm, tub seal) mean the tub and drum come apart, and that is where we compare the quote with you.
  • The condition of the rest of the machine. A sound tub, motor and drum on a front-load or top-load washer make a single-part repair worthwhile.
  • The quote against the price of a comparable new washer. We give you the exact repair price after diagnosis so the comparison is real.
  • Parts availability for your model. Discontinued parts or a long backorder change the answer.

Usually worth diagnosing and repairing

These are the everyday washer repairs: one failed part, replaced on site, normally in a single visit.

  • A washer leaking water: a front-load door boot gasket, a drain hose or a water inlet valve.
  • A washer that won't drain: a drain pump or a coin trap and drain filter.
  • A washer that won't spin or won't start: a lid switch or door lock, a motor coupling, a drive belt, a shift actuator or a clutch assembly.
  • A washer not filling: a water inlet valve or a water level (pressure) switch.
  • A washer shaking or vibrating: shock absorbers on a front-load or suspension rods on a top-load machine.
  • A timer, main control board or touchpad board on a machine whose tub, motor and drum are sound.

When replacement may make more sense

  • The tub bearing, motor and control board are failing together.
  • The repair quote comes close to the price of a comparable new washer.
  • Parts for your model are discontinued or on a long backorder.

The Major teardown repairs group (tub bearing, spider arm, tub seal) is the decision point. The tub and drum have to come apart for those jobs, so when the diagnosis lands there we put the quote next to the price of a comparable new washer with you before anything is done.

faq.q: Is a leaking washer worth repairing?
faq.a: Usually yes. A leak normally comes from a front-load door boot gasket, a drain hose or a water inlet valve, which is a one-visit repair on a machine whose tub, motor and drum are sound. We quote the exact repair after diagnosis, before any work begins.

faq.q: My washer won't drain or spin. Repair or replace?
faq.a: Repair, in most cases. A washer that will not drain usually needs a drain pump or a cleared coin trap and drain filter. A washer that will not spin usually needs a lid switch or door lock, a motor coupling, a drive belt, a shift actuator or a clutch assembly. Each of those is a single part on an otherwise sound machine.

faq.q: When does a teardown repair change the decision?
faq.a: The Major teardown repairs group covers the tub bearing, the front-load spider arm and the tub seal. Those jobs need the tub and drum taken apart, so when the diagnosis lands there we compare the quote with the price of a comparable new washer with you before any work begins.

faq.a: Typical total repair cost (parts + labor) is $150–$450 on our washer repair page, depending on the part. The estimated labor by repair is listed there as labor only, parts extra, and every completed repair carries our 60-day parts and labor warranty.

dryer.title: Repair or Replace a Dryer? A Denver Guide
dryer.description: No heat, no start or a noisy drum? How we decide whether a dryer is worth repairing, what a diagnosis costs and when replacing makes more sense.
dryer.heroText: No heat, no start and a noisy drum are usually a one-part repair. Here is how we help you decide, with the exact price before any work begins.
dryer.body:
The short answer

Diagnose first. A dryer that runs without heat, will not start or squeals usually has one failed part in its heating circuit or drive, and one part on a dryer whose drum, motor and controls are sound is normally worth repairing.

Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price after diagnosis, before any work begins, and you compare that number with the price of a comparable new dryer.

Repair vs. replace at a glance

How repairing compares with replacing a dryer. Prices are never guessed: the repair side is quoted after diagnosis, the replace side is the price of a comparable new dryer.
FactorRepairReplace
Cost to find out$109 service call, which covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward the repair when you approve it.The price of a comparable new dryer.
What the price is based onThe part that failed and the labor to replace it, quoted after diagnosis and before any work begins.The model you choose: size, features and finish set the price, not the fault.
Installation and fitThe dryer stays on its vent and its outlet or gas connection; a stacked or laundry-closet unit is repaired where it stands.A new dryer has to match the vent position, the outlet or gas connection and, for a stacked pair, the washer beneath it.
How many major parts have failedOne failed part on an otherwise sound dryer is a normal repair.Several major components failing at the same time make a repair harder to justify.
Parts availabilityA part we can get is a repair we can quote.Parts that are discontinued or on a long backorder tip the decision toward replacing.
Warranty60-day parts and labor warranty on the completed repair.Whatever warranty comes with the new unit.

What to weigh before you decide

  • What failed. A thermostat, thermal fuse, heating element, belt, roller or idler pulley is one part. The drum, motor and controls failing together is a different situation.
  • Airflow. Long drying times and overheating are often an airflow problem, which a vent cleaning and a worn-part replacement normally solve.
  • Installation. A stacked or laundry-closet unit would be awkward to swap out, which tips a single-part fault toward repair.
  • The quote against the price of a comparable new dryer. We give you the exact repair price after diagnosis so the comparison is real.
  • Parts availability for your model. Discontinued parts or a long backorder change the answer.

Usually worth diagnosing and repairing

These are the everyday dryer repairs: one failed part, replaced on site, with the dryer staying where it stands.

  • A dryer not heating: a heating element on an electric dryer, a thermal fuse, or a high-limit or cycling thermostat.
  • A dryer that won't start: a thermal fuse, a door switch, or a power cord or terminal block.
  • A dryer making noise: drum rollers, an idler pulley, a blower wheel or a drum felt seal.
  • A dryer that takes too long or is overheating: an internal exhaust vent cleaning, a moisture sensor bar or a blower wheel.
  • A dryer that won't tumble: a drive belt, an idler pulley or a drive motor.
  • A stacked or laundry-closet unit that would be awkward to swap out.

When replacement may make more sense

  • The drum, motor and controls are failing together.
  • The repair quote comes close to the price of a comparable new dryer.
  • Parts for your model are discontinued or on a long backorder.

A dryer with poor airflow is not a replacement case on its own: a vent cleaning and a worn-part replacement normally solve it, and we check the airflow as part of the diagnosis.

A note on gas models. The decision works the same way for a gas or an electric dryer: one failed part on a sound machine is normally worth repairing, and the drum, belt, rollers, idler pulley, blower and airflow parts are the same on both. The heating parts differ, so tell us which type you have when you book. For gas dryers: if you smell natural gas near the dryer at any point, do not attempt to operate the machine or test components. Leave the area, avoid operating any electrical switches, and contact your gas utility provider's emergency line from outside the building.

faq.a: Usually yes. A dryer that tumbles without heat most often has one failed part in its heating circuit: a heating element on an electric dryer, a thermal fuse, or a high-limit or cycling thermostat. We replace the part on site and quote the exact repair after diagnosis, before any work begins.

faq.q: My dryer squeaks or thumps. Repair or replace?
faq.a: Repair, in most cases. Noise usually comes from drum rollers, an idler pulley, a blower wheel or a drum felt seal, each a single wear part on a dryer whose drum, motor and controls are sound.

faq.q: Does a stacked or laundry-closet dryer change the decision?
faq.a: Yes. A stacked or laundry-closet unit would be awkward to swap out, so a single failed part on one of those is normally worth repairing where it stands.

faq.q: How much does it cost to find out whether my dryer can be repaired?
faq.a: Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price before any work begins.

faq.q: What does dryer repair cost in Denver?
faq.a: Typical total repair cost (parts + labor) is $100–$400 on our dryer repair page, depending on the part. The estimated labor by repair is listed there as labor only, parts extra, and every completed repair carries our 60-day parts and labor warranty.

dishwasher.title: Repair or Replace a Dishwasher? A Denver Guide
dishwasher.description: Leaking, not draining or not cleaning? How we decide whether a built-in dishwasher is worth repairing, what a diagnosis costs and when the tub makes replacing the better call.
dishwasher.heroText: Most dishwasher faults are a pump, valve, latch, element or gasket. Here is how we help you decide, with the exact price before any work begins.
dishwasher.body:
The short answer

Diagnose first. A dishwasher that leaks, will not drain, will not start or leaves dishes wet usually has one failed part behind it, and one part on a built-in unit already fitted to your cabinets and plumbing is normally worth repairing.

Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price after diagnosis, before any work begins, and you compare that number with the price of a comparable new dishwasher. A cracked or rusted-through tub is the one fault that points to replacing.

Repair vs. replace at a glance

How repairing compares with replacing a dishwasher. Prices are never guessed: the repair side is quoted after diagnosis, the replace side is the price of a comparable new dishwasher.
FactorRepairReplace
Cost to find out$109 service call, which covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward the repair when you approve it.The price of a comparable new dishwasher.
What the price is based onThe part that failed and the labor to replace it, quoted after diagnosis and before any work begins.The model you choose: size, features and finish set the price, not the fault.
Installation and fitA built-in dishwasher stays fitted to your cabinets, water line and drain.A new dishwasher has to match the cabinet opening, the panel or finish, and the existing plumbing and power.
How many major parts have failedOne failed part on an otherwise sound dishwasher is a normal repair.Several major components failing at the same time make a repair harder to justify.
Parts availabilityA part we can get is a repair we can quote.Parts that are discontinued or on a long backorder tip the decision toward replacing.
Warranty60-day parts and labor warranty on the completed repair.Whatever warranty comes with the new unit.

What to weigh before you decide

  • What failed. A drain pump, inlet valve, door latch, heating element or gasket is one part. The pump, motor and control board failing together is a different situation.
  • Leaks. A leak from a gasket, hose or door seal is worth repairing promptly rather than living with; it is normally a single-part fix.
  • The tub and frame. A tub or frame that is cracked or rusted through cannot be fixed with a part swap, and that is when replacing makes more sense.
  • Fit. A built-in unit is already fitted to your cabinets and plumbing. A replacement has to match the opening and the connections.
  • The quote against the price of a comparable new dishwasher. We give you the exact repair price after diagnosis so the comparison is real.

Usually worth diagnosing and repairing

These are the everyday dishwasher repairs: one failed part, replaced on site, with the dishwasher staying in its cabinet.

  • A dishwasher that won't drain or holds standing water: a drain pump, a drain hose, an air gap or check valve, or a food chopper.
  • A dishwasher leaking: a door gasket or tub seal, a float switch or a general leak repair.
  • A dishwasher not cleaning: a circulation pump or wash motor, a spray arm or a diverter motor.
  • A dishwasher not drying: a heating element, or a thermal fuse or high-limit thermostat.
  • A dishwasher that won't start: a door latch or safety switch, an electronic control board or a touchpad board.
  • A dishwasher making noise, or a rack adjuster, tine row clip or detergent dispenser.
  • A built-in unit already fitted to your cabinets and plumbing.

When replacement may make more sense

  • The tub or frame is cracked or rusted through.
  • The pump, motor and control board are failing together.
  • The repair quote comes close to the price of a comparable new dishwasher.

Parts for your model that are discontinued or on a long backorder also tip the decision toward replacing. We tell you which case you are in after the diagnosis, before anything is quoted or done.

faq.q: Is a leaking dishwasher worth repairing?
faq.a: Usually yes, and promptly. A leak normally comes from a door gasket or tub seal, a hose or a float switch, which is a single-part repair on a built-in unit already fitted to your cabinets and plumbing. We quote the exact repair after diagnosis, before any work begins.

faq.q: My dishwasher won't drain. Repair or replace?
faq.a: Repair, in most cases. Standing water usually means a drain pump, a drain hose, an air gap or check valve, or a food chopper, each a single part on an otherwise sound dishwasher.

faq.q: When is a dishwasher not worth repairing?
faq.a: When the tub or frame is cracked or rusted through, when the pump, motor and control board are failing together, or when the repair quote comes close to the price of a comparable new dishwasher. We tell you which case you are in after the diagnosis.

faq.a: Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price before any work begins.

oven.title: Repair or Replace an Oven, Stove, or Range? A Denver Guide
oven.description: Not heating, a dead burner or a door that will not close? How we decide whether a wall oven, range or cooktop is worth repairing, what a diagnosis costs and when to replace.
oven.h1: Repair or Replace an Oven, Stove, or Range?
oven.heroText: Heating, burner and door problems are usually a single-part repair. Here is how we help you decide, with the exact price before any work begins.
oven.body:
The short answer

Diagnose first. An oven that will not heat, a burner that stays cold or a door that will not close usually has one failed part behind it, and one part on an otherwise sound wall oven, range or cooktop is normally worth repairing.

Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price after diagnosis, before any work begins, and you compare that number with the price of a comparable new range or wall oven. Damage to the oven cavity or frame is the one fault that points to replacing.

Repair vs. replace at a glance

How repairing compares with replacing an oven, stove or range. Prices are never guessed: the repair side is quoted after diagnosis, the replace side is the price of a comparable new range.
FactorRepairReplace
Cost to find out$109 service call, which covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward the repair when you approve it.The price of a comparable new range.
What the price is based onThe part that failed and the labor to replace it, quoted after diagnosis and before any work begins.The model you choose: size, features and finish set the price, not the fault.
Installation and fitA wall oven, slide-in range or cooktop stays fitted to its cabinet cutout, countertop or wall.A new wall oven or cooktop has to match the cutout and the connection; a freestanding range is the easiest to swap.
How many major parts have failedOne failed part on an otherwise sound oven, stove or range is a normal repair.Several major components failing at the same time make a repair harder to justify.
Parts availabilityA part we can get is a repair we can quote.Parts that are discontinued or on a long backorder tip the decision toward replacing.
Warranty60-day parts and labor warranty on the completed repair.Whatever warranty comes with the new unit.

What to weigh before you decide

  • What failed. A bake or broil element, temperature sensor, burner switch, door hinge or gasket is one part. The control board, elements and sensors failing together is a different situation.
  • Which type you have. A built-in wall oven, slide-in range or cooktop is fitted to your cabinets, which tips a single-part fault toward repair. A freestanding range is simpler to replace.
  • The cavity and frame. An oven cavity or frame that is damaged beyond a part swap is when replacing makes more sense.
  • The quote against the price of a comparable new range or wall oven. We give you the exact repair price after diagnosis so the comparison is real.
  • Parts availability for your model. Discontinued parts or a long backorder change the answer.

Usually worth diagnosing and repairing

These are the everyday oven, stove and range repairs: one failed part, replaced on site, with the appliance staying in its cutout.

  • An oven not heating: a bake or broil element, an oven temperature sensor or a control board.
  • An oven temperature that is inaccurate: an oven temperature sensor or a control board.
  • A burner not working on an electric cooktop: a coil burner, a glass-cooktop radiant element or a burner control switch.
  • An oven door that won't close: a door hinge, a door gasket or door glass.
  • An oven that won't turn off or a self-clean cycle that no longer runs on an otherwise sound oven.
  • A convection or cooling fan motor, an indicator light or switch, a drip bowl or a terminal block.
  • A built-in wall oven or slide-in range fitted to your cabinets.

When replacement may make more sense

  • The oven cavity or frame is damaged beyond a part swap.
  • The control board, elements and sensors are failing together.
  • The repair quote comes close to the price of a comparable new range.

Parts for your model that are discontinued or on a long backorder also tip the decision toward replacing. We tell you which case you are in after the diagnosis, before anything is quoted or done.

A note on gas models. The decision works the same way for a gas, electric or dual-fuel model: one failed part on a sound oven or range is normally worth repairing, and the door, hinge, gasket, glass and most controls are the same on both. The burner and ignition parts differ, so tell us which type you have when you book. If you smell gas when attempting to use the oven, or at any time near the appliance, do not operate the oven, do not operate any electrical switches, and do not attempt to light the oven manually. Leave the area, ventilate without using fans, and contact your gas utility's emergency line from outside the building.

faq.q: Is an oven that won't heat worth repairing?
faq.a: Usually yes. An oven that will not heat most often has one failed part: a bake or broil element, an oven temperature sensor or a control board. We replace the part on site and quote the exact repair after diagnosis, before any work begins.

faq.q: Should I repair or replace a built-in wall oven?
faq.a: A built-in wall oven is fitted to a cabinet cutout, so a single failed part on an otherwise sound unit is normally worth repairing. Replacing it means matching the cutout and the connection. We give you the exact repair price after diagnosis so you can compare it with the price of a comparable new wall oven.

faq.q: One burner on my cooktop stopped working. Repair or replace?
faq.a: Repair, in most cases. On an electric cooktop a cold burner usually means a coil burner, a glass-cooktop radiant element or a burner control switch, each a single part. Tell us whether your cooktop is gas or electric when you book.

faq.q: When should I replace a range instead of repairing it?
faq.a: When the oven cavity or frame is damaged beyond a part swap, when the control board, elements and sensors are failing together, or when the repair quote comes close to the price of a comparable new range. We tell you which case you are in after the diagnosis.

faq.q: How much does it cost to find out whether my oven can be repaired?
faq.a: Our $109 service call covers the visit and diagnosis and is credited toward your repair when you approve it. You get the exact repair price before any work begins.

faq.q: What does oven repair cost in Denver?
faq.a: Typical total repair cost (parts + labor) is $150–$500 on our oven repair page, depending on the part. The estimated labor by repair is listed there as labor only, parts extra, and every completed repair carries our 60-day parts and labor warranty.
